report:
The original completion criteria are not met. The argument establishes the restricted continuous-positive-Hessian criterion and the examples A–D, but neither establishes that hypothesis for arbitrary continuous F nor constructs two different supports for the actual B_0. No concrete mathematical defect was found in the restricted proofs. E correctly states their scope. This submission leaves the original question unresolved; this is not a claim about its current literature status.

A. The bounded-product and linearization argument is valid under its explicit antecedent. The continuous complex Hessian gives a continuous Euclidean Laplacian locally. Cutting off its right-hand side and subtracting a Newtonian potential gives W^{2,p} regularity for every finite p; the remaining distribution is harmonic. Sobolev embedding gives the stated C^{1,α} representatives, and canonical uniqueness identifies these with the genuine potential. After adding a smooth local ρ with dd^cρ≥ω, positive radial regularizations decrease to the bounded psh potential. Their complex Hessians converge uniformly on smaller balls. Applying bounded Bedford–Taylor continuity to every degree, then expanding the fixed smooth correction ω−dd^cρ, identifies the actual nonclosed-background product with σ^n. This uses no undefined product of rough currents. The same construction applies to u+th for both signs of sufficiently small t.

The density F_t is continuous and strictly positive after exponentiation, and u+th actually solves its equation with scalar c_0(F). Scalar uniqueness therefore gives B_0(F_t)=B_0(F). The supporting inequality yields ∫(F_t−F)dν≤0. The uniform determinant expansion F_t−F=t tr_σ(dd^ch)+O(t²), applied with both signs, proves stationarity of every support. Only uniqueness of the scalar is used, not uniqueness of the potential.

B. The continuous-coefficient Fredholm proof survives reconstruction. The rational constant-coefficient symbols are smooth at zero and satisfy the stated multiplier bounds uniformly when the frozen matrices range through a compact uniformly elliptic family. Freezing on sufficiently small charts absorbs coefficient oscillation. Cutoffs introduce only lower derivatives, and the mollifier interpolation estimate absorbs the first derivatives. This establishes the global W^{2,p} estimate uniformly along L_s.

The maximum-principle passage uses the correct regularity. Smooth annular approximation converges uniformly up to the boundary, while operator errors converge in L^{2n}; ABP therefore passes to W^{2,p} when p>2n. For the tangent-ball barrier, L_sφ=e^{−k|y|²}(4k²a^{ij}y_i y_j−2k tr a)>0 on the annulus for sufficiently large k. Comparison of w−εφ forces a positive inward derivative at a zero minimum of the C¹ function w, a contradiction. The requisite tangent ball can be chosen near a boundary point of the zero set inside a coordinate chart. This proves the strong maximum principle, the constant kernel of L_s, and the trivial kernel of L_s−1 without differentiating coefficients.

The compactness contradiction for the uniform inverse estimate is also valid: residual convergence and strong L^p convergence make the normalized sequence Cauchy in W^{2,p} by the preceding estimate. Its nonzero limit would lie in ker(L_s−1). The smooth starting operator has index zero by a smooth elliptic deformation to a negative-sign Laplace–Beltrami operator minus one, and has trivial kernel by the maximum principle. If one starts with its classical Hilbert-space Fredholm realization, smooth-data solvability and the already proved inverse estimate extend it to all L^p data. Openness follows from the Neumann lemma; closedness follows from the uniform estimate and compactness. Finally, the inclusion W^{2,p}→L^p is compact, so L_σ has index zero and a one-dimensional range annihilator.

The duality choice is correct: q=1+1/(4n)<n/(n−1), and p=q/(q−1)=4n+1>2n. The task-granted density bounds put every support in L^q. Smooth density and Hölder duality extend stationarity to W^{2,p}. All support densities then lie in the same one-dimensional annihilator, and mass one identifies them. The derivative argument is valid as well: nonempty probability supports at both inputs already imply the uniform-norm Lipschitz bound. Every weak cluster of supports at F+tH supports F, so uniqueness and the two supporting inequalities give the claimed two-sided directional derivative. No Fréchet conclusion follows from this argument.

C. The product construction meets A's antecedent. The sphere Green kernel G(x,z)=log d_ch(x,z)^2+1 has dd^c_xG=δ_z−w and mean zero. Its uniformly integrable logarithmic singularity makes the Green solution for A−a bounded and continuous. Its distributional Hessian is exactly (A−a)w; the canonical representative is genuine. Pullback gives σ=Aw+bκ>0, and the actual product is (k+1)Ab^k w∧κ^k. Thus c_0(F)=1.

For an arbitrary smooth test h on the whole product, integrating A^{−1}L_wh against (A/a)w⊗ν_κ cancels A and gives base Stokes for each vertical slice. Integrating b^{−1}L_κh gives zero by vertical stationarity for each base point. Fubini therefore establishes full-test stationarity, not merely separated-test stationarity. The candidate has a bounded density; the one-dimensional annihilator and an existing actual support identify it with that support. Consequently it satisfies the defining inequality for every continuous G. Gauduchon's smooth theorem is applied only to κ when k≥2; its even-Betti surface hypothesis from Theorem 1 is irrelevant. For k=1, Stokes gives ν_κ=κ.

D. The Hopf form descends under z↦2z and is smooth and positive on the compact quotient. With s=|z|², dd^c(s^{−1})∧dd^cs=0 follows from s(s^{−1})''+2(s^{−1})'=0. Hence dd^cκ=0, and ∫L_κh κ²=2∫dd^ch∧κ=0. With κ₀=|z|^{−2}dd^c|z|², direct radial integration over 1≤|z|≤2 gives ∫κ₀²=4 log 2. Thus κ=(4 log 2)^{−1/2}κ₀ and the support is explicitly (A/a)w∧κ².

The Hopf quotient is S³×S¹, so H²(Y,R)=0. A hypothetical Kähler form would be exact and have positive square integral, contradicting Stokes; restricting a Kähler form on the product would contradict this on Y. The horizontal-one/vertical-two component db∧κ of dω is nonzero and cannot cancel the purely vertical component b dκ. Also 0≤f≤1, so A≥a−ε>0, b≥1, and exp(F)=3Ab² stays strictly positive. Along a transverse equatorial arc, the logarithmic A contribution is bounded below by a positive multiple of 1/log(e/r), whereas the smooth b contribution is O(r). This proves the divergent Dini integral and failure of every positive Hölder exponent for F. The reference remains the original nonsingular zero.

The earlier determinant note n1 is a valid partial reduction under the task's current representation. Its matrix equality case, Fatou rank exclusion, inverse-shape moment bound, and equivalence between probability equality and equality of the absolutely continuous matrix parts all check out. They do not establish constancy of θ. Its two-site construction has no geometric current realization and supplies no Hermitian counterexample.

The artificial-functional note n2 also checks out at its stated scope. The lacunary-series error estimate tends to zero relative to the kth amplitude, and the one-third oscillation sets contradict coincidence with a C¹ function on a positive-measure set via density points. The proposed densities satisfy the supporting inequality, all supports have the stated bounds, and the zero-set argument establishes the dense G_delta uniqueness set. At F=H the two displayed measures have sine moments 0 and 1/8. This concerns B_art, which is never identified with B_0.

S07 is an overlap comparison, not a premise of A–D. Its explicit envelope, continuous residual product, signed-measure resolvent, harmonic-mode identification, approximation limits, and displayed numerical example reconstruct correctly conditional on its separately declared singular normalization/support framework. The resolvent argument obtains uniform approximants for both the function and its Laplacian, so it does not assume an unspecified rough generator core. Its pole-filling limit correctly retains divisor mass. That singular framework is not granted by the original task and is not established by this audit. The nonsingular two-curve overlap follows directly from the residual operator and probability formulas; no priority conclusion is needed.

Harmless corrections: Taylor's compact inclusion is equation (6.9), not 'Proposition 6.9'; Demailly's radial regularization is located in I.4.18/I.5.5, with canonical distributional identification in I.5.8. The supplied Taylor nonlinear-elliptic excerpt concerns harmonic maps and does not verify ABP; the retrieved actual §13, Proposition 13.1 and Lemma 13.2 do. The initial 'no proof ... is supplied' header is obsolete because complete drafts follow it. These corrections do not require a new mathematical argument.

passages.statement: On an open subset Ω of C^n, a distribution v whose complex Hessian is positive has a unique locally integrable plurisubharmonic representative. For a locally integrable psh function, nonnegative radial smoothing kernels of mass one give smooth psh regularizations on smaller domains that decrease to its genuine representative as the smoothing radius decreases to zero.

For a locally integrable psh function, nonnegative radial smoothing kernels of mass one give smooth psh regularizations on smaller domains that decrease to its genuine representative as the smoothing radius decreases to zero.

For locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions v_1,…,v_k on Ω⊂C^n, k≤n, the Bedford–Taylor currents dd^c v_1∧…∧dd^c v_k are defined recursively by distributional dd^c, are symmetric and multilinear, and converge weakly when each v_i is approached by a pointwise decreasing sequence of locally bounded psh functions with locally bounded psh limit.

If a smooth Fourier multiplier symbol P on R^m satisfies |D^αP(ξ)|≤C_α〈ξ〉^{−|α|} for every |α|≤m+1, then P(D) is bounded on L^p(R^m) for every 1<p<∞.

For 1<p<∞, smooth functions are dense in W^{2,p} on compact smooth manifolds without boundary and on smooth bounded Euclidean domains. Smooth bounded domains admit bounded W^{2,p} extension operators. In real dimension m, W^{2,p} embeds continuously into C^{1,α} when p>m and 0<α≤1−m/p, and its inclusion into L^p is compact on these compact manifolds and bounded domains.
passages.quote: The space C∞c(Rn+) of smooth functions is dense in Wk,p(Rn+).

A smooth elliptic differential operator P of order r on a compact smooth manifold without boundary is Fredholm from H^{s+r} to H^s for every real s. Its distributional solutions are smooth wherever their right-hand sides are smooth, and local smooth-coefficient elliptic regularity also holds in L^p Sobolev spaces for 1<p<∞.

For a smooth positive Hermitian metric κ on a connected compact complex manifold Y of complex dimension k≥2, the formal adjoint of L_κ=tr_κ(dd^c) has a one-dimensional smooth kernel generated by an everywhere strictly positive function. Consequently there is a unique smooth positive probability ν_κ satisfying ∫_Y L_κh dν_κ=0 for every smooth real h. No parity condition on the first Betti number is required.
